description: Add the DynamoDB tooling and run against DynamoDB Local; this feature is where the FEAT-003 driver first meets a real engine. This is plan.md items 9-11 and design.md sections 8.1 (DynamoDB harness), 8.3/8.3.1, 9.1, 9.2, 9.4, 9.5 and 10, with [F31] (credential pre-flight), [F32] (migrate exit code for an unreachable endpoint) and [F33] (refusal text, stray tokens, quoting). It adds: db/dynamoTables.ts (parseTablesArgs, assertLocalEndpoint, ensureAppTable, runTables); the DynamoHarness; the opt-in DynamoDB contract block; dynamoOnly.test.ts; the DynamoDB block of seed.test.ts; db/migrateSqliteToDynamo.ts plus its test; db/cli.ts plus cli.test.ts; the migrate.ts and reset.ts driver guards; the dynamo:tables and dynamo:migrate scripts (backend plus root aliases); and the docker-compose dynamodb profile. The contract must pass on DynamoDB Local with 0 skipped; fix driver bugs it reveals in FEAT-003 files. Depends on FEAT-001, FEAT-002 and FEAT-003.
steps: Create packages/backend/src/db/dynamoTables.ts per design §9.5. TablesArgs. parseTablesArgs: only --reset, anything else throws CliPreconditionError with usage. assertLocalEndpoint(endpoint): presence only; when absent throw CliPreconditionError('Refusing: dynamo:tables only targets DynamoDB Local (set DYNAMODB_ENDPOINT). Cloud tables come from infra/ (CDK).'). ensureAppTable(client, tableName, { reset }): DescribeTable; on a key-schema or GSI-name mismatch throw CliPreconditionError 'run with --reset'; reset deletes, waits and recreates; create uses buildCreateTableInput and waitUntilTableExists (maxWaitTime 60). runTables(cfg, argv): parse, assertLocalEndpoint before any client, print table/endpoint/action (created|exists|recreated), destroy the client in finally.

In packages/backend/src/test/repositoryHarness.ts add DynamoHarness and dynamoHarness(endpoint) per §8.1. tableName = `UrbaniTest${Date.now().toString(36)}${4 random hex}App`, fixed at construction. Construction is lazy, with no I/O. setupSuite creates the context (config.aws.region) and calls ensureAppTable. fresh(now) purges with a paginated ScanCommand plus batchWriteAll deletes, then calls createDynamoRepositories(ctx, { now }). cleanup is a no-op. teardownSuite deletes the table and destroys the client. context() throws before setupSuite. scanAll() returns every item. Never use config.db.dynamodb.tableName in tests.

Add to packages/backend/src/repositories/repositories.contract.test.ts: `const endpoint = process.env.DYNAMODB_ENDPOINT;` and `describe.skipIf(!endpoint)('repository contract [dynamodb] (set DYNAMODB_ENDPOINT to run)', { timeout: 20_000 }, () => defineRepositoryContract(dynamoHarness(endpoint!)));`.

Create packages/backend/src/repositories/dynamodb/dynamoOnly.test.ts: skip-if-no-endpoint, 20 s timeout, its own dynamoHarness. Cover: an oversized-evidence alert is stored trimmed and logs a warn; an over-limit non-alert item raises ITEM_TOO_LARGE; one test calls every create path once (upsertRole, upsertUser, first preferences.update, audit.record, alerts.insert, upsertLivePreservingStatus on a new id, services.upsert, environments.ensure, the three upsertMany, aiAnalyses.insert, integrations.upsert, createSession, appendMessage, first setFeedback). Then scanAll() has entityType in ENTITY_TYPES on every item, all 16 values appear, the live alert has entityType 'ALERT', and the prefs item has userId.

Add the DynamoDB block to packages/backend/src/db/seed.test.ts: skip-if-no-endpoint, 20 s timeout, its own dynamoHarness. beforeEach calls setRepositoriesForTesting(await harness.fresh(makeTestClock())); afterEach calls resetRepositories() and harness.cleanup(). Assert the same counts as the SQLite block, and that a second seed() leaves them unchanged.

Run on DynamoDB Local. Plan.md V7 pre-flight: stop if credentials are found. V8.1-V8.2: docker run amazon/dynamodb-local:2.5.2 on 127.0.0.1:8000 and wait for 'CorsParams'. V8.3: $env:DYNAMODB_ENDPOINT='http://127.0.0.1:8000'; npm test must pass with 0 skipped. Fix driver bugs in the FEAT-003 files and never weaken a contract case. If a GSI-dependent case flakes, add the design §15.5 bounded retry (at most 1 s) in the harness only. Then V8.7 (docker stop).

Create packages/backend/src/db/migrateSqliteToDynamo.ts with every design §10 export. parseMigrateArgs(argv, baseDir?): no fs access; --source required; --dry-run and --allow-aws allowed; a missing value, unknown flag or stray token throws CliPreconditionError [F33]; path.resolve(baseDir ?? process.env.INIT_CWD ?? process.cwd(), raw). Also MIGRATION_ENTITIES, EntityCounts, MigrationReport and SqliteSnapshot. readSqliteSnapshot(db) uses PRAGMA table_info: a 001-only source gets role SUPER_ADMIN, result SUCCESS or FAILURE when metadata.outcome==='unavailable', and missing new tables count as 0 rows; evidence and actions ORDER BY ordinal; links come from the alert_id columns. migrateSqliteToDynamo(...): create-only writes in dependency order with concurrency 8; users use TransactWriteItems with emailLockItem ([0] failed = skipped; [1]-only failed = failed plus a conflict log with ids only); the dry run uses batchGetAll; the evidence budget feeds trimmedEvidence; every item comes from the items.ts builders. runMigrate(cfg, argv) checks in order: parse; console.log('Source (read-only): <abs>'); statSync isFile ('--source is not a regular file: <abs>'); without an endpoint and without --allow-aws throw CliPreconditionError('Refusing: dynamo:migrate would target AWS DynamoDB. Pass --allow-aws, or set DYNAMODB_ENDPOINT for DynamoDB Local.') before opening the file or creating a client; new Database(source, { readonly: true, fileMustExist: true }); health.ping, where a fatal PersistenceError exits 2 with 'create the table first (npm run dynamo:tables)' or the access hint and a non-fatal UNAVAILABLE logs 'DynamoDB not reachable at <endpoint>' and returns 1 [F32]. Then console.table per entity and logger.info('Migration summary', report). Return 1 if totals.failed > 0, else 0. Destroy the client in finally.

Create packages/backend/src/db/migrateSqliteToDynamo.test.ts per the §8.3 row. Default suite: readSqliteSnapshot on in-memory 001-only and 002 databases. Opt-in block with its own dynamoHarness, writing through harness.context() and reading through the harness repositories: a dry run reports counts and scanAll() is []; a real run creates items (spot-check evidence, links and the user lock with entityType 'USER_EMAIL'); every scanned item has entityType; preferences, chat sessions, messages and feedback read back equal to the SQLite repositories' output for the source; a re-run reports everything skipped; relatedMetricIds survive. Re-run the opt-in suite on DynamoDB Local (V7, V8.1-V8.3, V8.7).

Create packages/backend/src/db/cli.ts per design §9.5. Its only top-level value imports are './cliErrors' and '../lib/errors'. export async function main(argv): Promise<number>. Step 1: argv[0] must be 'tables' or 'migrate', otherwise usage on stderr and return 2. Step 2: const { config } = await import('../config'); on throw print the message on stderr and return 2. Step 3: import ../lib/logger and the command module, then runTables or runMigrate. Step 4: map CliPreconditionError -> logger.error(message) -> 2; a fatal PersistenceError -> logger.error(..., { awsError, hint }) -> 2; anything else -> logger.error('<command> failed', { message }) -> 1. Last line: `if (require.main === module) void main(process.argv.slice(2)).then((code) => process.exit(code));`.

Create packages/backend/src/db/cli.test.ts per §8.3.1. Pure functions are imported statically: parseTablesArgs rejects unknown flags; assertLocalEndpoint(null) throws and 'http://dynamodb-local:8000' passes; parseMigrateArgs requires --source and rejects unknown flags, missing values and a stray token [F33]. Source resolution against base, INIT_CWD or cwd; absolute paths unchanged. Six main() cases, each after `vi.resetModules(); const { main } = await import('./cli');` with process.env snapshot/restore and vi.mock('../repositories/dynamodb/client') recording no createDynamoContext call for ['tables'] without an endpoint. The AWS-refusal case asserts exit 2 AND the exact [F33] text via a process.stderr.write spy. Temporary files only under fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'urbani-cli-')).

packages/backend/src/db/migrate.ts: add `import { config } from '../config'`. In the CLI block (line 60), before runMigrations(), when config.db.driver !== 'sqlite', logger.info('No SQL migrations for DB_DRIVER=dynamodb (table schema: dynamo:tables / IaC)') and process.exit(0). packages/backend/src/db/reset.ts: the first statement of reset() (line 13), before the production guard and getDb(), throws Error('reset is SQLite-only. For DynamoDB Local run `npm run dynamo:tables -- --reset`') when config.db.driver !== 'sqlite'.

packages/backend/package.json scripts: "dynamo:tables": "ts-node src/db/cli.ts tables" and "dynamo:migrate": "ts-node src/db/cli.ts migrate". Root package.json scripts: "dynamo:tables": "npm run dynamo:tables --workspace @urbani/backend --" and "dynamo:migrate": "npm run dynamo:migrate --workspace @urbani/backend --". docker-compose.yml: add the §9.1 dynamodb-local service (image amazon/dynamodb-local:2.5.2, profiles ["dynamodb"], command ["-jar","DynamoDBLocal.jar","-sharedDb","-inMemory"], ports "127.0.0.1:8000:8000", networks urbani_net) after the frontend service and before `volumes:` (line 87). Leave the backend service unchanged.

Run the verification below in its stated order. Record the evidence in this FEAT's findings. Commit on dpi2, e.g. `feat(backend): DynamoDB Local tooling, opt-in integration tests and SQLite->DynamoDB migration`.

With DynamoDB Local running and DYNAMODB_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:8000, `npm test` exits 0 with 0 skipped; 'repository contract [dynamodb]' passes all 69 cases.

The plan.md V9 guards hold: dynamo:tables without an endpoint exits 2; dynamo:migrate without an endpoint or --allow-aws exits 2 with the exact [F33] text; DYNAMODB_ENDPOINT=ftp://x exits 2 naming DYNAMODB_ENDPOINT; seed with DB_DRIVER=dynamodb and no endpoint exits 2; reset with DB_DRIVER=dynamodb exits 1 naming dynamo:tables -- --reset; and no guard creates .tmp\smoke\guard\unused.sqlite.

Plan.md V8.4-V8.5: dynamo:tables creates the table; the seed runs twice without error; the migrate dry run prints 'Source (read-only): <abs>' and the same would-create counts twice with 0 would-skip; a real run creates and a re-run skips everything.
The DynamoDB Local container is stopped and removed afterwards, and ports 4100 and 8000 are free.

NOTES FOR LATER STEPS.
- CLI behaviour, for the docs (FEAT-005). `npm run dynamo:tables [-- --reset]` prints 'Table <name> at <endpoint>: created|exists|recreated'. An existing table whose key schema or GSI1 (name and key schema) differs from tableDefinition.ts exits 2 with 'Table <name> does not match the app table definition (key schema or GSI1); run with --reset'; --reset deletes, waits and recreates any existing table. A failing DynamoDB Local call (e.g. ECONNREFUSED) exits 1 ('tables failed' { message }). `npm run dynamo:migrate -- --source <path> [--dry-run] [--allow-aws]`; compiled form `node packages/backend/dist/db/cli.js <tables|migrate> ...`. Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 when any item failed, when the target is not reachable (non-fatal UNAVAILABLE at the ping, logged 'DynamoDB not reachable at <endpoint>'), or on an unexpected error ('<command> failed' { message }); 2 on usage, configuration and precondition errors and on a fatal store error ('<command> failed: Persistence store unavailable' { awsError, hint }; hint 'create the table first (npm run dynamo:tables)' for ResourceNotFoundException, otherwise 'check the AWS credentials and the table access policy'; ops.translateAwsError logs its own 'DynamoDB call failed' line first).
- Interpretation choices where the design text was not explicit (behaviour-preserving; please review): (1) ensureAppTable applies --reset before the definition check, so --reset can repair a mismatched table. (2) runMigrate turns a failed read-only open into CliPreconditionError 'Cannot open --source read-only: <abs> (<reason>)', exit 2, per design §10 'each failed check exits 2'; an empty or non-SQLite file still opens and fails at the first read (exit 1). (3) parseMigrateArgs: the --source value must be non-empty and must not start with '--'; a second --source and the '--source=<path>' form are usage errors. (4) During writes an UNAVAILABLE PersistenceError aborts the run (safe to repeat); any other per-item error, and any row that fails to map, is counted failed and logged 'dynamo:migrate: item failed' { entity, id, error: reason or error name }. A user whose email lock belongs to another user is counted failed and logged 'dynamo:migrate: email lock owned by another user' { entity: 'users', id }. (5) trimmedEvidence counts alerts created (would-create in a dry run) with trimmed evidence, not skipped ones. (6) console.table prints one table with a row per entity plus a TOTAL row; dry runs label the columns wouldCreate/wouldSkip, while the 'Migration summary' JSON keeps created/skipped with dryRun: true. (7) readSqliteSnapshot detects missing tables through sqlite_master and missing columns through PRAGMA table_info.
- The V6 source database is in WAL mode with -wal/-shm sidecars after the smoke; it opened read-only without a copy.
- cli.test.ts reads stderr through a process.stderr.write spy and parses the logger's JSON lines, so the exact refusal text is compared against each line's 'message'.
- Each opt-in block creates and deletes its own UrbaniTest<runId>App table. A test run killed midway can leave such a table in a long-running DynamoDB Local container (in memory; gone when the container stops).
- Shell tool: a call that prints nothing for a while is cut off with ^C (seen with `npm test | Select-Object -Last N`, `| Out-File` and `docker stop`). Stream instead: `2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" } | Tee-Object -FilePath <abs>`, and re-check `docker ps -a` after an interrupted docker stop. npm propagates the script's exit code (2) through both npm layers, and a --source path containing a space survives the root alias.
- Port check: while the container runs, Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8000 -State Listen shows nothing for the Docker Desktop port forward even though a TCP connect succeeds, so V10's port check alone proves nothing for 8000. Pair it with `docker ps -a --filter name=urbani-dynamodb-local` and a TCP connect probe.
- Design §15.4 (Compose failing on ${JWT_SECRET:?} when JWT_SECRET is unset) was not tested; the check set JWT_SECRET=dev as documented.
- OBSERVATION (not caused by this step, left untouched): the MAIN workspace C:\Antigravity\Urbani DPI still shows ' M .gitignore' with --untracked-files=no (first recorded by FEAT-001).
